messages:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a short smoke of fused-attn variants on the 1B seq=1024 profile, focusing on QKV packing + bias/rope fusion. results are odd, posting raw logs.

jin: nice, did you compare FlashAttention v1 vs v2 vs our fused path? :eyes:

alex: yep. gave FlashA v1 (baseline), FlashA v2 (algo tweak), and fused-qkv (our kernel with qkv packing + epilogue fused ops). also tried paged-attn with 32k page size for kv.

maria: any regressions in latency P95? that's what triggered the last rollout alert.

alex: P95 numbers below, single stream (no batching) on A10x2:
```
model: 1B, seq=1024, batch=1, device: 2xA10
FlashA-v1: p50 18.2ms, p95 32.1ms, throughput 555 tok/s
FlashA-v2: p50 16.8ms, p95 29.0ms, throughput 590 tok/s
fused-qkv: p50 14.9ms, p95 35.8ms, throughput 620 tok/s
paged-attn(32k): p50 17.2ms, p95 33.4ms, throughput 560 tok/s
```

sam: fused-qkv p95 is worse than v2 even though p50 improves — looks like tail jitter. did you profile kernel stalls? :thinking:

alex: yes. `nvprof`/triton trace shows more frequent kernel preemption at long seqs for fused-qkv. KV cache page faults? Not real page faults but memory fragmentation causing extra memcpy in epilogue path.

jin: can you paste the trace snippet for the fused epilogue?

alex: paste:```
[TRC] fused_qkv_epilogue_kernel 0.34ms -> 26 launches per batch
[TRC] memcpy_async (kv_cache_write) 0.8ms -> occasional spikes up to 12ms
[TRC] cudaSync linger 0.9ms when swapping pages
```

maria: that memcpy_async spike matches last week's incident where a model bump increased rope bias tensor shape, causing extra mem copies. did you try disabling bias/rope fusion to isolate?

alex: yes — toggled bias/rope fusion off (keeps qkv packing). results: p95 drops to 30.1ms, throughput 610 tok/s. so bias/rope fusion contributes to the tail.

jin: interesting — so bias/rope fusion reduces p50 but amplifies tail due to extra epilogue bookkeeping. is that bookkeeping coming from shape checks or from KV writes?

alex: looks like shape normalization + conditional path for rope application when cache pages are hot vs cold. that conditional causes branch divergence on GPU and extra device->device memcpy in our current KV layout.

sam: we probably need a deterministic epilogue path with vectorized rope apply (no branch) or precompute rotated rope for cached segments. tradeoffs?

maria: precomputing rope for every possible offset is expensive memory-wise. but we could precompute per-page rope vectors when a page is first loaded (amortize cost). that would move spikes to page load time, which is rare.

alex: agree. also other low-effort change: reorder writes to use fused memcpy+compute (single kernel) instead of memcpy_async + separate epilogue kernel. that might reduce cudaSync and kernel launch overhead.

jin: did you test batched case? our autoscaling decisions rely on batching heuristics.

alex: quick batched test batch=8, seq=256 typical convo case:
```
FlashA-v2: p50 8.6ms, p95 12.3ms, throughput 6.8k tok/s
fused-qkv: p50 7.1ms, p95 16.7ms, throughput 7.4k tok/s
```
fused-qkv still has tail in batched workload. suggests per-request epilogue variance accumulates under batching.

sam: that explains why autoscaler saw throughput drop under load — scheduler saw many long requests and scaled down batch size. we need a heuristic: if epilogue variance > 2x median, force smaller per-device inflight windows.

maria: or a more general solution: make kernel chooser prefer FlashA-v2 for latency-SLO routes, fused-qkv for cost-oriented routes where median matters. we already route by policy but kernel chooser lacks a tail-awareness metric.

jin: can we add a simple tail penalty score: tail_score = log(p95/p50) and add to cost function when choosing kernel? low perf % of requests route to fused-kernel if tail_score > threshold.

alex: implemented local sim: fused-qkv tail_score=2.4, FlashA-v2 tail_score=1.7. using threshold=2 moves ~18% of traffic to v2 which stabilizes service p95 by ~15%.

sam: that's a good mitigation short-term. long-term we should fix the fused epilogue. action items?

maria: 1) alex: prototype page-level precompute for rope + single-launch epilogue kernel (owner: alex, due EOD next Tue).
2) jin: add kernel chooser tail_score and a canary config flag (owner: jin, due this Fri).
3) infra-bot: run nightly perf sweep on 1B/2B models with seq buckets [128,512,1024,2048] and report regressions.

infra-bot: got it — scheduling nightly sweep, will post results to #eng-runtime/perf-results tomorrow. (reacted with :white_check_mark:)

alex: also logging small repro harness in repo: `tools/perf/repro/fused-epilogue-smoke.py` with a toggle to force rope on/off. pushing in a sec.

jin: perfect. once jin's chooser flag is live we can route high-SLA customers off fused-qkv until the epilogue fix lands.

maria: agree. thanks team — prioritize test infra and epilogue fix. dropping notes into the perf checklist. :thumbsup:

sam: saved convo and will add to the regression runbook.

alex: will follow up with trace snippets and a small flame graph snapshot later today.
